definitions.explanation: Used to refer to the fifth day of a calendar month.
A span of five days, often in the form {五日間|いつかかん}.

examples.japanese: {五月|ごがつ}{五日|いつか}はこどもの{日|ひ}だ。
{来月|らいげつ}の{五日|いつか}に{会議|かいぎ}がある。
examples.english: There's a meeting on the 5th of next month.

examples.japanese: {毎月|まいつき}{五日|いつか}には{給料|きゅうりょう}が{振|ふ}り{込|こ}まれる。
examples.english: My salary is deposited on the 5th of every month.

examples.japanese: {五日間|いつかかん}{出張|しゅっちょう}に{行|い}く。
examples.english: I'm going on a five-day business trip.

examples.japanese: あれから{五日|いつか}{経|た}った。
examples.english: Five days have passed since then.

examples.japanese: {連休|れんきゅう}は{今年|ことし}も{五日間|いつかかん}{続|つづ}く{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: This year too the consecutive holidays are scheduled to last five days.

notes:
{五日|いつか} uses the native Japanese counting series for days 1–10 of the month: {一日|ついたち}, {二日|ふつか}, {三日|みっか}, {四日|よっか}, {五日|いつか}, {六日|むいか}, {七日|なのか}, {八日|ようか}, {九日|ここのか}, {十日|とおか}. The same forms also count durations in days (except {一日|いちにち} for 'one day' as a duration).

DISAMBIGUATION:
Do not confuse with いつか (someday, sometime), which is written either in kana only or with kanji {何時|いつ}か. The two are unrelated despite the identical reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {五月|ごがつ}{五日|いつか}: May 5th (Children's Day)
- {毎月|まいつき}{五日|いつか}: the 5th of every month
- {五日間|いつかかん}: five-day period
